title: How the knight moves

D0.outcome: Says that the knight jumps in an L (two squares one way and one square at a right angle) and may jump over pieces.

D1.outcome: When told 'knight', marks every square the knight can jump to: it cannot land on its own pieces but may take an enemy piece there.

D2.outcome: In a busy position where the piece is not named, marks every square the knight can reach, including from the edge and the corner.

D3.outcome: Finds the fewest knight jumps between two squares and names a route.

misconceptions: A piece standing between the knight's start and landing square blocks it.
The knight always has eight moves, even on the edge or in the corner.
conditions: The knight jumps two squares along a rank or file and one at a right angle; pieces in between do not matter.
It cannot land on its own piece but may take an enemy piece.
contrasts: On the edge or in a corner the knight has fewer than eight landing squares.
Pieces standing next to the knight do not block it.

soft_prereq_notes.FND.PIECE.QUEEN.D1: taught after the sliding pieces (rook, bishop, queen and king) so that the knight is met as the one piece that jumps over others
